newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Succession issue vital for Yugoslavia - paper.
newsitem.headline: Succession issue vital for Yugoslavia - paper.

text.p: Division of assets of the former Yugoslavia is a key issue in settling Belgrade's international position and it wants to make a constructive contribution, Belgrade daily Politika reported on Thursday.

"Yugoslavia, wishing to make a constructive contribution to negotiations (on succession), sees room in certain areas for talks on a partial division of property, the division of archives for instance," the paper quoted a Yugoslav commission statement as saying.

This was in line with the draft memorandum on succession sent by international mediator Arthur Watts, the Yugoslav government commission for cooperation with the Peace Implementation Council and international financial and trade organisations said.

It will be difficult for expert groups to resolve the succession issue because former Yugoslav republics wish to settle problems of succession partially and give them a political rather than an economic dimension, the commission said.
The former Yugoslav states are due to continue succession talks under international mediation in Brussels early in June. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +381 222 43 05
